dronepal.manual.name: Corvus Field Manual
dronepal.manual.subtitle: Companion Drone · Field Manual
dronepal.manual.landing: A companion drone that fits in a Curios slot: it follows you, mounts a gun, scans, lights the ground, carries cargo and talks.$(br)Every number here comes from the current mod data.$(br)No network, no language model, and it never edits the world.
dronepal.manual.p.what.1: Corvus is a companion drone that lives in a Curios slot.$(br)Put the terminal into the Drone slot and the airframe appears at your shoulder; take it out and it is stowed again.$(br)Modules, battery, gun and cargo are all stored in the terminal, so recalling never loses anything.
dronepal.manual.p.what.2: It does exactly four things: follow you, look for you, fight for you and carry for you.$(br)It will not mine, place blocks or craft for you.$(br)Abilities come from modules. Without the module the ability simply does not exist; it is not merely switched off.
dronepal.manual.p.deploy.1: $(li)Press G, open Curios, and drag the terminal into the Drone slot.$(br)$(li)A terminal that only sits in your backpack never deploys; right-clicking in hand just reminds you to slot it.$(br)$(li)Once deployed it follows you, and holds position while you turn on the spot.$(br)$(li)Removing the terminal from the slot recalls the drone; everything inside is kept.
dronepal.manual.p.deploy.2: $(li)Stand close, empty-handed, hold Shift and right-click the airframe to open its panel.$(br)$(li)Drag battery, modules, gun and ammo into their slots; Shift-click moves stacks between panel and inventory.$(br)$(li)Hover a module for its full numbers.$(br)$(li)With no battery every module goes offline; only following and hovering remain.
dronepal.manual.p.controls.1: Hold V for the control wheel. Its eight sectors map to eight actions:$(br)$(li)North: follow / hold position; recall when there is no signal$(br)$(li)North-east: weapon auto / safe$(br)$(li)East: cycle engagement policy$(br)$(li)South-east: scan patrol (needs a scan module)
dronepal.manual.p.controls.2: $(li)South: medic on / off$(br)$(li)South-west: carry on / off; hold Shift to deliver now$(br)$(li)West: light on / off$(br)$(li)North-west: link on / off; hold Shift to pass a magazine$(br2)Shift on East cycles fire mode (Combat Mk.III only). Shift on North recalls.$(br)Move the mouse and release to act; if you already clicked while it was open, releasing only closes it.
dronepal.manual.p.station.1: The assembly bench is the only place that builds subsystems, cores, modules, batteries and airframes.$(br)A crafting table cannot make them; only the bench blueprints can.
dronepal.manual.p.station.2: $(li)Pick a target in the blueprint list on the left; a green dot means the materials are complete.$(br)$(li)Scroll to page, or use the arrows to step one by one.$(br)$(li)Nine input slots; load them and press Start.$(br)$(li)A job takes 80 ticks (about 4 seconds) and keeps running after you close the screen.$(br)$(li)Breaking the bench refunds the materials in full.
dronepal.manual.p.parts.1: Airframe: 4 iron ingots + 2 copper ingots.$(br)Servo motor: 3 copper ingots + 2 redstone + 1 iron ingot.$(br)Nearly every blueprint starts with these two.
dronepal.manual.p.parts.2: Circuit board: 1 gold ingot + 4 redstone + 2 quartz.$(br)Battery cell: 2 copper ingots + 2 redstone + 1 paper.
dronepal.manual.p.parts.3: Optics: 2 glass + 1 amethyst shard.$(br)Heat sink: 2 iron ingots + 1 blue ice; combat and medical parts need it.
dronepal.manual.p.parts.4: Armour plate: 3 iron ingots + 1 leather.$(br)Medical supply: 1 sugar + 2 paper + 1 redstone, consumed by White Crow treatment.$(br)Spray can: 1 iron ingot + 1 gunpowder + 1 matching dye, nine paints in all.
dronepal.manual.p.first.1: Build these in the assembly bench, bottom up:$(br)$(li)Flight controller: 2 circuit boards + 1 servo + 1 gold ingot$(br)$(li)Speed controller: 1 circuit board + 2 servos + 1 copper block$(br)$(li)Powertrain: 2 cells + 1 speed controller + 1 airframe$(br)$(li)Sensor array: 2 optics + 1 circuit board
dronepal.manual.p.first.2: $(li)Peregrine airframe: 2 airframes + 1 powertrain + 1 flight controller + 1 sensor array + 1 glass$(br)$(li)OmniDrive 100 battery: 3 cells + 1 airframe$(br2)The first build costs roughly 50 iron and 46 copper, plus quartz, amethyst, gold and a piston. This is a mid-game project.
dronepal.manual.p.frames.1: Peregrine (standard)$(br)span 1.45 · 3 module slots · 6 ammo slots$(br)80 HP · 10 damage per hit max$(br)pistol / SMG / rifle / sniper$(br)Built at the assembly bench.$(br2)Owl (recon)$(br)1.10 · 2 slots · 4 ammo$(br)56 HP · 8 max$(br)pistol / SMG$(br)Military supply crates.
dronepal.manual.p.frames.2: Bedrock (heavy)$(br)1.80 · 4 slots · 8 ammo$(br)144 HP · 12 max$(br)every gun type, RPG included$(br)Military supply crates.$(br2)Patchwork (converted)$(br)1.35 · 3 slots · 6 ammo$(br)64 HP · 10 max$(br)pistol / SMG / rifle$(br)Scrap blueprint or salvage crates.
dronepal.manual.p.frames.3: How to choose:$(br)Peregrine is the balanced prototype and does a bit of everything.$(br)Owl is small and quick, good for early scouting, but only takes small guns.$(br)Bedrock is the toughest, has the most slots and takes an RPG, at the cost of weight and poor solar efficiency.$(br)Patchwork is cheap to fly, but it leaks power and may malfunction.
dronepal.manual.p.quirks.1: Follow-teleport threshold / cooldown:$(br)Peregrine 16 blocks / 40 ticks$(br)Owl 13 / 20$(br)Bedrock 24 / 80$(br)Patchwork 18 / 60, with an 8 percent chance to fail.$(br2)Solar factor: Owl and Peregrine 1.0, Patchwork 0.9, Bedrock 0.6.
dronepal.manual.p.quirks.2: Acceleration response / knockback resistance:$(br)Owl 1.25 / 0.05$(br)Peregrine 1.0 / 0.3$(br)Patchwork 0.9 / 0.25$(br)Bedrock 0.75 / 0.85$(br2)Mount capacity: Owl 0.6, Peregrine and Patchwork 1.0, Bedrock 1.6.$(br)A Patchwork airframe has a 5 percent malfunction chance for 60 ticks; Rustnail cells also leak.
dronepal.manual.p.modules.1: Seven families, one module of each per drone:$(br)$(li)combat: mounts a gun and fires it$(br)$(li)scan: marks mobs and ores$(br)$(li)carry: picks up and delivers$(br)$(li)medic: heals and cures
dronepal.manual.p.modules.2: $(li)light: lights the ground around you$(br)$(li)link: ammo and hit reports, passes magazines$(br)$(li)solar: recharges while it sees the sky$(br2)Slot count follows the airframe: Owl 2, Peregrine 3, Patchwork 3, Bedrock 4.$(br)A second module of the same family is refused. Unmount the gun before removing the last combat module.
dronepal.manual.p.modules.3: Combat drain / range / burst / effective spread:$(br)$(li)Anvil Mk.I 14 / 16 / 3 / 4.8 deg$(br)$(li)Anvil Mk.II 18 / 20 / 4 / 3.2 deg$(br)$(li)Anvil Mk.III 22 / 24 / 5 / 2.0 deg$(br)$(li)Rustnail G1 10 / 12 / 2 / 9 deg, and it jams
dronepal.manual.p.modules.4: Medic idle / treating / per use / cooldown:$(br)$(li)White Crow Gen1 4 / 12 / 6 / 40 s$(br)$(li)White Crow Gen2 6 / 16 / 8 / 30 s$(br)$(li)White Crow Gen3 8 / 20 / 12 / 20 s$(br)$(li)Rustnail G1 5 / 14 / 6 / 30 s, one in five causes nausea
dronepal.manual.p.modules.5: Light drain / level / radius: 2/12/8, 3/15/12, 4/15/16 (Mk.III works underwater).$(br)Solar clear / rain / night FE/t: 8/2/0, 12/4/0, 16/6/2.$(br)Cargo slots / pickup radius: 9/6, 18/8, 27/10.$(br)Link drain: 3/5/7.
dronepal.manual.p.sourcing.1: The three civilian families (carry / light / solar) are built at the bench:$(br)$(li)Cargo core: 1 airframe + 1 chest + 2 servos$(br)$(li)Luma core: 1 optics + 2 glowstone dust + 2 copper ingots$(br)$(li)Solar core: 2 optics + 3 copper ingots + 2 glass panes$(br)Mk.I = 1 matching core + 1 airframe
dronepal.manual.p.sourcing.2: $(li)Mk.II = 1 matching Mk.I + 1 upgrade kit$(br)$(li)Mk.III = 1 matching Mk.II + 1 advanced upgrade kit$(br2)Upgrade kit: 2 circuit boards + 1 copper block + 1 amethyst shard.$(br)Advanced kit: 3 circuit boards + 1 diamond + 1 netherite scrap + 2 heat sinks.$(br)Upgrades go one tier at a time; another vendor is not a valid stepping stone.
dronepal.manual.p.sourcing.3: Six Rustnail G1 parts are bench-built from scrap: trigger, rangefinder, basket, styptic, headlamp and panel.$(br)Military and medical parts only come from crates or trade:$(br)$(li)Military crate 42%%: pillager outpost / stronghold corridor / end city$(br)$(li)Salvage crate 35%%: abandoned mineshaft / shipwreck supply / large underwater ruin$(br)$(li)Medical crate 30%%: village temple / igloo$(br)$(li)Cleric: White Crow Gen1/2/3 for 12/24/36 emeralds
dronepal.manual.p.batteries.1: The battery decides how long you can fly.$(br)Fit it into the battery slot in the panel; without one every module is offline.$(br)Each airframe caps battery tier: Owl and Patchwork at tier 2, Peregrine and Bedrock at tier 3.
dronepal.manual.p.batteries.2: Capacity / receive rate:$(br)$(li)OmniDrive 100/200/300: 180k / 350k / 600k FE, 300/400/500$(br)$(li)Corvus R-1/R-2: 150k / 300k FE, 400/500$(br)$(li)Anvil Mk.I/II/III: 250k / 600k / 1.2M FE, 600/800/1000$(br)$(li)Rustnail G1/G2: 280k / 560k FE, 420/560
dronepal.manual.p.batteries.3: Rustnail cells leak every 10 seconds: 2 or 3 percent chance, losing 5 or 6 percent of charge.$(br)Vendor drain factors: OmniDrive 0.85, Anvil 1.1, Rustnail 0.75, Corvus and Alba 1.0.$(br)Below one fifth charge the hungriest module switches itself off and the HUD turns red; at zero only following and hovering remain.
dronepal.manual.p.charging.1: Charging dock: 6 iron ingots + 2 copper ingots + 1 redstone.$(br)Right-click with a battery (or a terminal carrying one) to insert; right-click empty-handed to take it back.$(br)A drone hovering above the pad also charges, writing into the battery inside the terminal.
dronepal.manual.p.charging.2: $(li)Buffer 32,000 FE$(br)$(li)Cable input 2,000 FE/t, scaled by chargeRateMultiplier$(br)$(li)Coal: 4,000 FE per lump, at most 200 FE/t, up to 64 lumps stored$(br)$(li)Battery receive caps run from 300 to 1,000 FE/t by model$(br)Breaking the dock drops its item and remaining coal.
dronepal.manual.p.guns.1: Requirements: a combat module, an airframe that accepts the gun, and the gun in an ammo slot.$(br)Gun limits:$(li)Owl: pistol / SMG$(li)Peregrine: pistol / SMG / rifle / sniper$(li)Patchwork: pistol / SMG / rifle$(li)Bedrock: everything, RPG included$(br)Ammo slots: Owl 4, Peregrine 6, Patchwork 6, Bedrock 8.
dronepal.manual.p.guns.2: Once it has a lock it turns immediately, so it can run with you and fire behind itself.$(br)The gimbal swings 75 degrees each side of the body and pitches independently; only past that does the body follow.$(br)The first engagement includes a deploy-to-level delay.$(br)Long guns fold within a length limit, so an RPG never pokes through the roof.
dronepal.manual.p.policy.1: Five policies: passive, hostiles only, retaliate, assist and aggressive.$(br)The default is retaliate: it answers only after you or the drone is hit.$(br)To clear mobs proactively, switch to hostiles only or aggressive.$(br)Every policy targets hostile mobs only; villagers, iron golems, allays, pets and teammates are never targets.
dronepal.manual.p.policy.2: Friend or foe is decided only by current FTB Teams membership; the owner is always protected.$(br)Bullets pass through neutral players, so standing between the drone and a zombie is safe.$(br)Hitting a player requires all of: server PvP enabled, /dronpvp enable then /dronpvp confirm, and a legal current target.$(br)/dronpvp off disables it.
dronepal.manual.p.scan.1: Effective scan radii include the Corvus 1.2 vendor bonus:$(br)$(li)Corvus R-1: 19 blocks, hostiles, 6 s$(br)$(li)Corvus R-2: 29 blocks, hostiles + coal/iron/copper, 10 s$(br)$(li)Corvus R-3: 38 blocks, hostiles + all ores, 20 s$(br)$(li)Rustnail G1: 14 blocks, hostiles, 4 s, 8 percent failure
dronepal.manual.p.scan.2: Ores show as cyan boxes, mobs as orange-red outlines, visible through walls and tracking their movement.$(br)It scans automatically every 15 seconds; the server option autoScanSeconds accepts 5 to 300.$(br)South-east on the V wheel toggles the patrol.$(br)Turning it off clears every mark at once.
dronepal.manual.p.maint.1: Destroyed or lost to the void: it rebuilds beside you after 30 seconds with everything in the terminal intact, and nothing drops.$(br)Owner death follows Curios rules; re-equip after respawn.$(br)Invulnerability lives in config/dronepal-server.toml as creative_owner (default), always or never, and hot-reloads on save.$(br)chargeRateMultiplier defaults to 1.0 and accepts 0.25 to 20.
dronepal.manual.p.maint.2: Commands:$(br)$(li)/dronepal who are you | battery | scan | heal | pass ammo$(br)$(li)/dronepal memory for the archive$(br)$(li)/dronepal pvp: enable then confirm, off to disable$(br)Offline dialogue also answers recipe, advancement and gun-data queries; see docs/OFFLINE-CONSOLE.md.$(br)The archive is keyed by terminal serial: first boot, time together, rebuild count.
